concepts.why: The patient's history of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla, severe pruritus, and lack of response to treatment with hydrocortisone cream and ketoconazole cream suggest an allergic reaction, which is consistent with contact dermatitis.
The patient's presentation of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion, limited to his right axilla, and severe pruritus is consistent with dyshidrotic eczema.

The patient's history of oval and annular thin violaceous patches in his right axilla, although not typical of seborrheic dermatitis, could be considered in the differential diagnosis given the lack of other findings.

The patient's presentation of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla, severe pruritus, and lack of response to treatment with hydrocortisone cream and ketoconazole cream could be consistent with nummular dermatitis.

The patient's history of severe pruritus and discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla could be consistent with atopic dermatitis, although the lack of other atopic features and the localized nature of the lesions make this less likely.

The patient's presentation of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion, limited to his right axilla, could be considered in the differential diagnosis of psoriasis, although the lack of other psoriatic features makes this less likely.

The patient's history of oval and annular thin violaceous patches in his right axilla could be consistent with tinea corporis, although the lack of other fungal features and the negative Wood lamp examination make this less likely.

The patient's presentation of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion, limited to his right axilla, could be considered in the differential diagnosis of lichen planus, although the lack of other lichenoid features makes this less likely.
It explains the biopsy finding of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction.
